biography.plain_text: Maroun Semaan was a Lebanese engineer and businessman who co-founded Petrofac International with Ayman Asfari. After managing Gulf infrastructure projects for Consolidated Contractors, he helped build the oilfield-services group from its Sharjah base. He later chaired Alcazar Capital, investing across renewable energy, telecommunications and property after retiring from Petrofac's executive leadership.

long_biography.plain_text:
A scholarship at the American University of Beirut helped Lebanese engineer Maroun Semaan complete his education. Raised in a village family that placed great importance on schooling, he later financed opportunities for other students through the Semaan Foundation. A university gift supported engineering and architecture research and educational facilities, and the faculty took his name.

His parents, Tanios and Souraya, were commemorated through a separate foundation gift to the university's medical centre. The funding supported an outpatient surgery centre for procedures that did not require an overnight hospital stay. Beyond his alma mater, the foundation backed Amideast scholarships, youth entrepreneurship initiatives and training for English-language teachers.
